archetypes.name: snapshot-tamper
archetypes.rationale: The change is security-motivated and depends on path reachability assumptions around pre-coder artifacts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the relocated pre-coder snapshot directory is actually protected from the external coder paths granted by the dispatch flow. Check whether any writer, fallback mode, or future caller can still tamper with pre-coder-head.txt, pre-coder-tracked-paths.txt, or pre-coder-path-diffs before carryover classification. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash32
archetypes.rationale: The diff changes shell helpers and eval-based tests where Bash 3.2 and strict-mode behavior can regress subtly.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the shell changes for Bash 3.2 compatibility, strict-mode hazards, quoting issues, and safe handling of derived snapshot paths. Pay attention to mkdir/write ordering, local variable initialization, process substitutions, and sed/eval function extraction in tests. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: step5-flow
archetypes.rationale: The relocation crosses review-and-fix, Step 5 telemetry, and MAV apply paths with different artifact ownership rules.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the integration between review-and-fix.sh, review-implement-step5-loop.sh, and MAV apply after the snapshot relocation. Verify that structural telemetry, coder-stage manifests, post-coder heads, and head-only MAV behavior still use the intended artifact locations without stale round_dir reads. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: resume-compat
archetypes.rationale: The change intentionally fails closed for old round artifacts, so resume and mixed-version behavior deserve focused review.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review how mixed old/new round directories behave when pre-coder snapshots exist only in the former round_dir location or are partially missing. Check whether fail-closed behavior creates acceptable outcomes for carryover classification, follow-up commits, cap handling, and recovery from interrupted rounds. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
